DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Paragraph Three Takes the Stand

STS-HS9-L3-13001400-HSELA910-MKT-IMR-01 • HS English Grade 9 • Organizing Ideas and Making Connections in Informative Writing
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In a real courtroom a lawyer cannot hand the judge a fact and sit down. She has to say what the fact proves and how it ties to everything the jury already heard. Amina, Farid, and Yulia are running that same test on an essay about three families who traveled a long way to get here. Every paragraph is an exhibit, and every exhibit needs a link that says why it belongs.
Exhibit B is the suitcase. What sentence would you say to connect the suitcase to the main idea of the essay?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Amina doing?
Look at the picture. Say what Amina is doing and explain why she is doing it in front of the others in two complete sentences. Use the exact word for her action, not general words like doing.
2
What is Farid holding?
Look at the picture. Say what Farid is holding and explain why he is holding it up for everyone to see in two complete sentences. Use the exact word for the object, not general words like thing.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Say what the teacher is doing and explain why she is doing it while the students talk in two complete sentences. Use the exact word for her action, not general words like working.
4
What kind of place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Say what kind of place this is and explain how you know in two complete sentences. Use the exact words for what proves it, not general words like place.
5
Tell me about the board on the easel.
Look at the picture. Say what is on the big white board and explain why someone put it there in two complete sentences. Use the exact words for what is on the board, not general words like stuff.
6
What is Yulia wearing?
Look at the picture. Say what Yulia is wearing and explain why she is the only one dressed that way in two complete sentences. Use the exact words for the clothing, not general words like clothes.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS W.9-10.2 — Write informative and explanatory texts, organizing complex ideas and making connections. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
